places.name: University of Tokyo (formerly Tokyo Imperial University)
places.connection: The university where Jiro studied aeronautical engineering.

places.name: Mitsubishi Internal Combustion Engine Works
places.connection: The factory where Jiro Horikoshi worked and designed the A5M and A6M Zero fighter planes.

places.name: Karuizawa
places.connection: The mountain resort town where Jiro meets, falls in love with, and later reunites with Naoko.

places.name: Junkers Factory (former location)
places.connection: Jiro visits this historic aircraft factory in Germany and is inspired by their advanced all-metal designs.

places.name: Studio Ghibli Museum
places.connection: The museum dedicated to the work of Studio Ghibli, the animation studio that produced the film.

places.name: Tokorozawa Aviation Museum
places.connection: Features exhibits on the history of Japanese aviation, including a replica of the A6M Zero.

places.name: Nihonbashi Bridge
places.connection: A key landmark depicted during the devastating 1923 Great Kantō earthquake sequence in the film.

places.name: Fujimi Kogen Hospital
places.connection: A real former sanatorium that served as the model for the one where Naoko receives treatment for tuberculosis.

places.name: Tomioka Silk Mill
places.connection: The landscape and architecture of this historic industrial site are reflected in the early scenes of Jiro's hometown.

places.name: Manpei Hotel
places.connection: Believed to be the model for the hotel where Jiro stays and meets the German character, Castorp.
